name: Break my Product
location: Homebrew Club, 111 Maiden Ln #540, San Francisco, CA 94108
description: Real users. Real feedback. Real product insights. Built something and want honest feedback before your next launch? In this interactive session, founders, builders, designers, and creators will be paired with each other to test products, uncover blind spots, and share actionable feedback. Here's how it works: Bring a product, prototype, MVP, or side project. Get matched with other participants. Watch as they explore, test, question, and intentionally try to "break" your product. Receive candid feedback on usability, clarity, onboarding, positioning, and overall experience. Return the favor by testing someone else's product. Whether you're validating a new idea, refining an MVP, or preparing for launch, you'll leave with fresh perspectives and a list of improvements you can act on immediately.

name: Break my Product 2.0
location: Homebrew Club, 111 Maiden Ln #540, San Francisco, CA 94108
description: Real users. Tougher testing. Better products. Built something and want brutally honest feedback before your next launch? We are back with an improved format designed to help founders uncover hidden issues, validate assumptions, and ship with confidence. Whether you're building an MVP, AI product, startup, side project, or prototype, this session gives you direct access to thoughtful testers who aren't afraid to ask hard questions. How it works: Bring a product, prototype, MVP, or side project. Get matched with fellow founders, builders, designers, and creators. Watch as they explore, test, question, and intentionally try to break your product. Receive candid, actionable feedback on usability, onboarding, messaging, UX, positioning, and overall product experience. Return the favor by testing someone else's product and sharing your own insights. This isn't a demo day—it's a collaborative product stress test. You'll leave with: Fresh perspectives from real users. A clearer understanding of where people get stuck. Actionable improvements you can implement immediately. New connections with builders who care about creating better products. Whether you're validating an idea, polishing an MVP, preparing for launch, or iterating after your first release, this is your chance to discover what works, what doesn't, and what to fix next.

name: Design & Deploy Workshop

You will learn a practical AI-powered workflow that you can use to quickly turn ideas into real products. name: Prompt to Production: AI Builders, Secure Code and Skills Workshop

You will build an application from a single prompt using AI, learn how AI can plan, code, test, and improve projects, identify and fix security issues in AI-generated code, publish your work as reusable AI Skills, explore how modern AI workflows are changing software development. name: BuildFest: Demos and Challenges
location: Sports Basement Outdoor & Camping, 1590, Bryant Street, Mission, San Francisco, California, 94103, United States
description: What if you could see 10 AI tools in action, try them yourself, and use them to solve real problems — all in one session? Buildfest: Demos and Challenges is a demo day, hands-on event where sponsors will show you what their tools can do, and then give you a small challenge to solve. No long workshops. No hours of setup. You’ll see → try → build → solve. Whether you're a developer, student, founder, designer, researcher, or just curious about AI, you can jump in at your level. Event Format You’ll start with a set of 10 sample datasets covering different real-world problems. You can choose one of them to work with, or bring your own dataset and problem. Pick a problem You can work on problems like: Build a system that creates study plans for students, Help shoppers find the right product based on their needs, Automate information extraction and processing from invoices, Build an AI travel planner, Summarize notes and extract important actions, Match candidates to jobs and help recruiters screen applications, Analyze restaurant data and identify inventory/demand problems, Build an AI system that answers common customer questions, Turn a simple idea into a structured content workflow, Find and evaluate promising problems and ideas or choose your own problem and build something that matters to you. How It Works Each sponsor will have a short demo + challenge. First, they'll show you their product in action and explain what it does, why it is useful, and how you can use it. Then you'll get a small challenge where you can try the tool yourself. You don't need to use every tool. Use whichever sponsor tools make sense for your problem — one, several, or all of them. The goal is to understand how each tool can be used and then combine the right tools to solve a problem.

name: Build your Co Founder Hackathon
location: 3120, Scott Boulevard, Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, 95050, United States
description: Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2–4 co-founders, combining humans and AI. Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder. You decide the rest—including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together. AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs. The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team—from idea to execution to a shipped product.
